channel.title: Installing Waydroid
channel.description: I am trying to install waydroid but there seems to be a kernel issue. I get a message that binder node vnd binder is not found. I have tried to mount it manually but get the message unknown file system type "binder". I would be grateful for any advice on how to deal with this issue, or at least to know whether or not it is possible to install waydroid. I realise it probably reduces security, but I am using a separate usb stick just for this and just want to get Signal and Whats app up and running.

item.title: Installing Waydroid
item.dc:creator: Jules
item.description:
A brief update - I determined that binder_linux is not compiled in the kernel but is available to load as a module with sudo modprobe binder_linux. However I still have the same problems. I think the binderfs is not mounting.

I have had further chats with the bot and it seems binderfs is not available in the kernel and so waydroid cannot work.

Read full topic

item.title: Installing Waydroid
item.dc:creator: Jules
item.description:
I installed from the debian backports repository, which has the latest version 1.6.3 - that is the route recommended by the waydroid site - their command sudo apt install waydroid -y. When I clicked on the icon the box came up to initialise it and install lineage and I got the message that binder node “vnd binder” could not be found. With chatbot’s help i tried to mount binderfs but then got the message unknown filesystem type “binder”.

This was my second attempt. The first time I initialised it on the command line and got a bit further that time but when i tried to start it on the command line I got a message "service manager /dev/anbox-binder has died.

I wondered if this binder_linux has been disabled as a security measure?

Read full topic
